title: Make a sticker-peel animation with sound in code
summary: A creator had Claude Code build a sticker-peel animation and its sound entirely in code, then joined them; they report a smooth 60-frames-per-second video with matching audio.
agent_role: Claude wrote the time-based rendering code for the animation and, from a separate prompt, the code-synthesized audio synced to frames. The human adapted a base prompt pack, supplied PNG artwork and directed the final combination.
outcome: Author reports a 60 fps animation with synced audio, shown in the post.
what_they_did: The creator started from a ready-made set of prompts called Opus 5.5 Motion Lab. It sets out how to draw each moment of the animation, move the paper and time each peel. They adapted the sticker stack to their own layers and supplied their own see-through images instead of having the model draw art. A separate prompt made the sound in code, timed to the frames. A video tool then joined picture and sound.
how_it_went: The author shows the finished video and describes it as 60 frames per second with flawless animation.
worth_knowing: Giving the agent your own images with see-through backgrounds, rather than asking it to draw artwork, does the cutting out for you. The method credits the Motion Lab prompt set and @seeconvm.
prompt: Build a code-rendered motion graphic of [describe the animation, e.g. a stack of stickers peeling off one by one]. Write a renderAt(t) function so every frame is a pure function of time, and render at [frame rate] fps for [duration] seconds. Use my transparent PNGs in [folder] as textures, with the alpha channel as each cutout. Do not draw the artwork yourself. Then write code that synthesizes a soundtrack synced to the key frames. Combine video and audio into an MP4 with ffmpeg. Show me a few preview frames before the full render.

curation.rationale: A real prompt-to-MP4 workflow with useful specifics: time-based rendering, PNG textures and ffmpeg muxing. It builds on someone else's prompt pack and resembles existing code-rendered video entries.
